newsitem.title: UK: Dollar floats up on raft of positive comment.
newsitem.headline: Dollar floats up on raft of positive comment.

text.p: The dollar firmed against the mark on Thursday after a raft of comments from German, French, U.S. and Japanese officials that they were comfortable with a strengthening U.S. currency.
In the latest of such statements, Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said he welcomed the dollar's recent improvement and would not mind if it strengthened further.

On European bourses, leading shares fell back in afternoon trading from opening highs that had been boosted by a sixth consecutive record close on Wall Street overnight. A weak opening in New York stocks on Thursday did nothing to help sentiment.
On the London exchange shares settled at lower levels in afternoon trading, unmoved by the latest batch of U.S. data, with the market preferring to dwell on signs of domestic inflationary pressures.

The blue chip FTSE 100 index was off 9.6 points at 3,917.3 by 1440 GMT after stronger-than-expected British retail price data wiped out early gains and fuelled fears that further UK interest rate hikes could be in the offing.

Analysts said Thursday's economic data from the U.S. was largely encouraging. Consumer prices and retail sales both rose in-line with most analysts expectations. But a fall in weekly jobless claims showed that labour market conditions were still tight.

Comments from Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke that policy would be set to meet the government's 2.5 percent target for underlying inflation reinforced worries that rates would have to go up again ahead of the next election.

"The mood the market has got itself into about interest rates, we're going to see a continuation of the jitters. If there wasn't an election coming up, rates would probably be higher than they are," said Panmure strategist Ian Williams.
The data were described by one economist as "truly awful".
In Frankfurt German shares ended bourse trade with modest gains despite earlier bouts of profit-taking following an early morning rally to record levels.
Dealers said the current level of the main DAX index was expected to hold firm ahead of the giant Deutsche Telekom flotation set for Monday.
The30-share DAX ended bourse trade up 3.58 points at 2,777.01 points.
On the Paris bourse French stocks were barely affected by the U.S. economic data but had fallen from morning highs into negative territory.

Main focus was insurers Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris as they requoted for the first time since announcing on Tuesday they planned to merge, creating the world's second largest insurance company.

UAP shares soared at the open, leaping 17.19 percent from their close on November 8. The stock was the biggest gainer in the market on huge volume. Axa meanwhile fell lower in smaller but still heavy volume as investors reacted to the expected dilution of Axa share value from the merger, which is set to occur through a stock swap.

On the currency markets, the firming of the dollar was aided not only by Tietmayer's comments but, earlier, by Japan's "Mr Yen", senior finance ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, who also welcomed a rising dollar.

"He is looking to re-establish the party line which is that the yen is not undervalued and that the dollar, potentially, has further to appreciate," Adam Chester, senior analyst at Yamaichi International said.

Among others to add their weight to the currency was U.S. Treasury Undersecretary Jeffrey Shafer, who said on Wednesday the new Clinton administration's aim had not changed and "Our policy is to have a strong dollar."

One focus of interest was the seemingly inexorable rise of the pound sterling, which was given a boost by the higher-than-expected UK inflation figures -- seen as a possible precursor to further British rate rises.

The pound was trading at a fresh four-year high against the dollar of $1.6650. It had already risen sharply on Wednesday after an unexpectedly large decline in UK jobless fuelled expectations of further rate rises. Traders said they saw $1.67 as the next psychological target.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5090 marks and 111.28 yen compared with 1.5041 marks and 111.38 yen late in Europe on Wednesday. The pound was at $1.6650.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 9.6 at 3,917.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 3.67 at 2,213.52.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 3.58 at 2,777.01.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $382.65 compared with $384.05 an ounce at the London close on Wednesday. Silver was two cents easier at $4.90. ($1=.6054 Pound)
